perspective:
From Christian Mensah’s available perspective, he knows/experienced:

- He is a police officer and has been close friends with Jonathan since childhood. He often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his perspective. Their favorite coffee shop is a familiar meeting place.
- Recently, Christian felt Jonathan was hiding something important, became anxious and suspicious, arranged a meeting, and confronted Jonathan.
- At the meeting, Christian told Jonathan he felt something was being hidden. He heard Jonathan say Christian could trust him.
- Christian observed Jonathan acting differently. Jonathan admitted he had been keeping something: he is in trouble and did not know how to tell Christian.
- Christian felt worried and empathetic, offered help, and said they could face it together. He heard Jonathan say the situation was complicated and he did not want to drag Christian into it.
- Christian told Jonathan he was his best friend and he would do everything he could to help. Jonathan said he could use support and resources and needed to find a way out.
- Christian came to believe Jonathan’s trouble might involve criminal activity. He asked Jonathan if it was illegal.
- Christian heard Jonathan say he could not say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he did not do anything illegal himself.
- Christian told Jonathan he would look into the matter discreetly. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Christian investigated and came to believe Jonathan was being framed. He told Jonathan this.
- Christian heard Jonathan react with shock and ask who would do such a thing. Christian said he was not sure yet, but had leads, and would gather evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence. Jonathan thanked him.
- Christian now believes the real culprit is someone close to both him and Jonathan, someone they both know and trust. He told Jonathan he found out who is behind it and planned to confront them and bring them to justice.
- Christian heard Jonathan warn him to be careful, call the person dangerous, and say he trusts Christian to do what is right.
- Christian has not, in the provided dialogue, told Jonathan the specific name of the culprit or the full details of his evidence.
